Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

**FIVE-SONS-OF-MAQABIS-OF-MOAB ROSTER** — the NUMBER-SYMMETRY WITH 1 MQ FIVE-BROTHERS. The five sons are named, paralleling the five-sons-of-Maqabis-of-Benjamin in 1 Mq (whose three named members are Abya + Sila + Fentos at 1 Mq seed 3:1 + γ.4.8.B 3:28). **The five-sons-of-Maqabis-of-MOAB roster is the STRUCTURAL MIRROR of the five-sons-of-Maqabis-of-BENJAMIN roster** — a NUMBER-SYMMETRY across the two books that is one of Horovitz 1905's clearest internal-structural-coherence evidences (Horovitz 1905 p. 195 fn. 4 + Frankfurt Codex Rüppel II 7 'Second Part' designation). Both books center their martyrdom-narratives on FIVE sons of a father-named-Maqabis; both have a sibling-warrior-strength theme; both have inter-locking refusal-speeches; both have post-mortem appearances. The structural-doubling supports the Horovitz-compositional reading that 1 Mq and 2 Mq derive from a single REDACTIONAL UNITY — perhaps the MOST STRUCTURALLY-SIGNIFICANT verse in the entire trilogy for scholarly-internal-coherence argumentation.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

MARTYRDOM-COMPLETION at 13:7-18 — sons' final-confessional speeches and execution. The chapter completes the dual-martyrdom-cycle structurally inaugurated at Ch 6 + Ch 9. Each son's final-speech is the SUMMATIVE-COVENANTAL-CONFESSION (creator + law + fathers + resurrection + reward + judgment of tyrant). The summative-confession pattern parallels: 4 MACCABEES 12:11-19 (youngest brother's elaborate final-speech); STEPHEN'S MARTYRDOM Acts 7 (the lengthy historical-recapitulation before death); MARTYRDOM OF POLYCARP 9-12 (Polycarp's confession-before-execution). Meqabyan's distinctive feature: the five-fold-speech-cycle completes at Ch 13 with structural-CALL-AND-RESPONSE to the five-fold opening at Ch 7 — the speeches function as ANTIPHONAL-TRIPTYCH spanning Chs 7 (refusal) + 9 (under-torture) + 13 (final-confession). Tewahedo homiletic tradition reads the triptych as the model-MARTYR-CONFESSIONAL-CYCLE that the Sǝnkǝsar saints' lives recapitulate.
